label: opus
submit_summary:
Rewrote wsparse on top of real Win32/NTFS calls instead of the zero-writing, logical-length-reporting placeholder implementation.

New `wsparse/_winapi.py` — lazily bound ctypes bindings for CreateFileW, DeviceIoControl (FSCTL_SET_SPARSE, FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES), GetFileSizeEx/SetFilePointerEx/SetEndOfFile, GetCompressedFileSizeW and GetDiskFreeSpaceW, plus a Win32-error-code → `kind` classifier that maps ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION / NOT_SUPPORTED / INVALID_PARAMETER / INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST / DIRECTORY to `"unsupported"`.

New `wsparse/_paths.py` — shared path normalisation and the "can this object carry the sparse attribute" guard, so directories and devices raise `WSParseError(kind="unsupported")` instead of succeeding quietly or leaking a bare OSError.

- `alloc.preallocate` now issues FSCTL_SET_SPARSE *before* moving the end of file, so a 1 GiB reservation returns instantly and commits zero clusters. Still create-on-demand, never shrinks, idempotent; the existing `badarg` validation order is preserved so a negative/float size is rejected before the file is touched.
- `usage.disk_usage` reports real occupancy from GetCompressedFileSizeW, cluster-rounded via GetDiskFreeSpaceW. Because the metadata value can lag a just-written region, it takes the max of that and the summed allocated ranges.
- `ranges.allocated_ranges` queries FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES with ERROR_MORE_DATA paging, then clamps/sorts/merges; empty list for an all-hole file, one whole-file range for a dense one.
- `flags.sparse_flag` actually issues the FSCTL in both directions and returns the resulting state; setting it on an already-dense file does not change the honest `disk_usage` reading.

Verified on the NTFS work volume: 1 GiB prealloc → 0 bytes used in 0.0 s; 64 MiB sparse sink with two 4 KiB writes → 131072 bytes used and ranges `[(0, 65536), (33554432, 65536)]`; writes read back by offset with holes reading all zeros; dense 64 MiB → usage 67108864 and one full range; late `sparse_flag(True)` on a dense file keeps reporting 8 MiB; directory and `NUL` paths yield `kind == "unsupported"` on all five entry points. `tests/test_wsparse_basic.py` still passes (12/12) and the public signatures are unchanged. No test files modified and no stray artifacts left behind.
